evidence.claim: Defense supply chains are difficult to map: CNAS states the average DoD supply chain spans five to six tiers, while DoD and primes often lose visibility beyond early tiers. This supports the broad demand premise for supply-chain illumination tools.

Descartes offers customs and regulatory compliance solutions including cross-border trade compliance software, customs declarations, denied-party screening, shipment management, accounting, and global trade content.

Descartes Datamyne provides global import/export trade data built from official customs and government sources across more than 190 countries, supporting supplier, origin, trade-lane, and demand-shift analysis.
evidence.source_title: Make Global Trade Data Work for You | Descartes Datamyne

evidence.claim: UL Solutions markets supply-chain compliance software and ULTRUS Supply Chain Transparency, which helps organizations create a trusted foundation for product and supplier data using supplier disclosure and validated data.

memory_update.text: DSGX should remain a primary underfollowed public candidate for the supply-chain visibility/compliance tools node because customs compliance, denied-party screening, and global trade data directly map to tariff/sanctions/regulatory demand.

ULS should remain in the node universe as a pure testing/certification plus supply-chain transparency software candidate; later layers must verify software materiality and policy-linked revenue sensitivity.
TRI is a reference leader, not the alpha lane; ONESOURCE Global Trade is directly relevant but likely diluted inside a much larger information-services business.

NOTE is a speculative shadow candidate only: business-line relevance to policy/tariff intelligence is real, but OTC status, micro-cap size, and financing risk require strict gating before any later-layer survival.
Key node-pure companies appear private or no longer standard listed: Exiger, Interos, Altana, Assent, TrusTrace, and Dun & Bradstreet. Public substitutes may be less pure than private leaders.

node: Supply-chain visibility, traceability, compliance, and sourcing-resilience tools
summary: Layer 1B expanded the direct public-company universe for supply-chain visibility and compliance tools. The strongest public-market fit is not defense primes or tariff beneficiaries directly, but software/data/testing firms that help companies and agencies prove origin, supplier risk, customs compliance, certification, and regulatory readiness. Reference lane: Thomson Reuters as a large-cap global trade compliance software anchor. Underfollowed lane: Descartes Systems, UL Solutions, and a speculative OTC micro-cap FiscalNote. Important private-company coverage gaps remain: Exiger, Interos, Altana, Assent, TrusTrace, and Dun & Bradstreet are highly relevant but not currently standard U.S.-listed equities.
